summary: Bradford's Instagram presence on social services spans pandemic response, homelessness, mental health, food security, reconciliation, and community inclusion. Bradford supports expanding shelters, supportive housing, mental health and addiction supports, and an outreach-first approach to encampments where shelter is offered before removal (DTu89cQjtBR, DMK2uOQgteh, DRCZSYbjSpb). Bradford frames addiction and mental health as provincial health-care responsibilities and argues the federal government should fund refugee shelter costs (DSZ7R5JgJZS, DQwumxDjYhU, CtW8t0Pp_Ix). Bradford backs investments in arts funding, the Tamil Community Centre, seniors programs, and Toronto Rent Bank as a permanent program (DCX1fRQNc0a, DHzTfsny-ut, CePKa3EuuIj). Bradford consistently expresses solidarity with 2SLGBTQ+, Jewish, Muslim, Indigenous, Tamil, Ukrainian, and Black communities and opposes hate-based discrimination (DJwW46pyNSo, CZU1A-COwLS, CqdUY-9Ag4L). During COVID-19, Bradford promoted targeted vaccine clinics in hot-spot neighbourhoods and mental-health fundraising for Michael Garron Hospital (CNctisNh0X6, CMXWtifhSrK).

key_positions.stance: Supports expanding shelters, supportive housing, and mental health/addiction supports while opposing long-term encampments; staff should offer shelter before any removal.
Frames addiction and mental health primarily as provincial health-care responsibilities and refugee shelter costs as a federal responsibility, arguing property taxes were not designed for these.
Supports investment in mental health programs and intergovernmental cooperation to build a supportive network of services.
Supports targeted vaccine distribution to hot-spot neighbourhoods and priority groups (frontline workers, teachers, seniors), and the City's vaccine mandate for employees.
Supports food security programming, food banks, and Out of the Cold meal services, while highlighting rising need.
Expresses solidarity with 2SLGBTQ+ communities and opposes homophobia, biphobia, and transphobia.
Stands in solidarity with Jewish, Muslim, Tamil, Ukrainian, and Black communities, and supports Holocaust education and anti-Islamophobia campaigns.
Supports truth and reconciliation work with First Nations, Inuit and Métis people, including the City's Reconciliation Action Plan and recognition of MMIWG2S.
Supports community-focused developments combining affordable rental housing, long-term care and seniors supports, and senior-focused programs like Meals on Wheels and Community Paramedicine.
Opposes provincial changes to the definition of disability that would reduce supports for Torontonians with disabilities.

Questions whether municipal property taxes should fund programs (school breakfasts, blanket library hour increases) that may be better delivered or scoped by other orders of government, while stating he is not seeking to cut them.
